history.heading: The Banda Oriental
paragraphs: Uruguay, between Argentina and Brazil, was inhabited by the Charrúa and other indigenous peoples, who resisted European settlement. Spain and Portugal contested the region, known as the Banda Oriental ("Eastern Bank") of the Uruguay River. The Portuguese founded Colonia del Sacramento in 1680, now a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and Spain founded Montevideo in 1726.

José Gervasio Artigas, the national hero, led the independence struggle from 1811. After occupation by Portuguese Brazil, Uruguay became independent in 1828 as a buffer state between Argentina and Brazil.

history.heading: The Switzerland of the Americas
paragraphs: The 19th century saw civil wars between the two traditional parties, the Blancos and Colorados. In the early 20th century, President José Batlle y Ordóñez built one of the first welfare states in the world, introducing secular education, the eight-hour day and divorce rights, earning Uruguay the nickname "Switzerland of the Americas".

Economic decline and the Tupamaros urban guerrilla movement led to a military dictatorship from 1973 to 1985, with mass imprisonment and torture. Democracy was restored in 1985. José Mujica, a former Tupamaro, was a famously modest president from 2010 to 2015.

culture.heading: Traditions
paragraphs: Spanish is the official language. Most Uruguayans are of European descent, especially Spanish and Italian, with an Afro-Uruguayan community whose candombe drumming is recognised by UNESCO. Uruguay is the most secular country in Latin America.

Drinking mate is a daily ritual, and asado (barbecue) is central to social life; Uruguay has one of the highest beef consumption rates in the world. Tango is shared with Argentina. Football is a passion: Uruguay won the first World Cup in 1930 and again in 1950, and won two Olympic gold medals.

politics.heading: Stable democracy
paragraphs: Uruguay is a presidential republic and one of the most stable and least corrupt democracies in Latin America. It has pioneered progressive laws, legalising same-sex marriage in 2013 and becoming the first country to fully legalise recreational cannabis in 2013. The left-wing Frente Amplio returned to power in 2025 with President Yamandú Orsi.

economy.heading: High-income economy
paragraphs: Uruguay has one of the highest incomes per person in Latin America and a large middle class. Exports include beef, soybeans, cellulose pulp, rice and dairy. Nearly all electricity comes from renewable sources, especially wind and hydropower. Tourism, IT services and logistics are growing. The currency is the Uruguayan peso.
